theme: God’s warning; Solomon’s foreign wives; the kingdom fractures
readingInstruction: Read 1 Kings 9:1-11:43. God appears to Solomon a second time with a warning. Then the story shows Solomon’s wealth, his many wives, and his fall into idolatry. Read chapter 11 with care. It is the end of the unit’s story.
settingTheScene: After the temple’s dedication, God appears to Solomon with a conditional promise and a warning. The following chapters describe Solomon’s accomplishments: cities, ships, the visit of the Queen of Sheba, and enormous wealth. Then, in chapter 11, the narrator gives a sad accounting of Solomon’s heart. The kingdom that began with wisdom ends in compromise. God announces the division of the kingdom, but for David’s sake, not all of it.
observation: God says, “If you will walk before me, as David your father walked… then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever” (9:4-5).
“But if you turn aside from following me… then I will cut off Israel from the land” (9:6-7).
The Queen of Sheba says, “The half was not told me. Your wisdom and prosperity surpass the report that I heard” (10:7).
“Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you” (10:9).
Solomon’s gold: 666 talents a year, ivory, horses, and chariots (10:14-29).
“King Solomon loved many foreign women… he had 700 wives, who were princesses, and 300 concubines. And his wives turned away his heart” (11:1-3).
“His heart was not wholly true to the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father” (11:4).

“Because you have done this… I will tear the kingdom from you… However, I will not do it in your days, for the sake of David your father… I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake of David my servant” (11:11-13).
interpretation:
God’s second appearance to Solomon repeats the pattern of the covenant: the promise is sure, but the individual’s blessing depends on obedience. “If you will walk before me… I will establish your throne. But if you turn aside… Israel will become a proverb and a byword among all peoples.” It is a clear warning, delivered right after the temple’s dedication.

Chapter 10 shows the glory. The Queen of Sheba comes from far away to test Solomon with hard questions. She is overwhelmed. Her response is one of the most moving praises in Kings: “Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you.” The nations are drawn to the wisdom of Israel’s king. For a moment, it looks as though the promise to Abraham is being fulfilled.

But the details are ominous. “Gold, ivory, horses from Egypt.” Deuteronomy 17:16-17 had warned the king not to acquire many horses, wives, or silver and gold. Solomon does all three. The narrator lists them with growing weight. What looks like prosperity is the accumulation of what he was told to avoid.

Chapter 11 is the tragic center. Solomon loved many foreign women, and they turned his heart away to other gods. The wisest man in Israel is a fool for love. He builds high places for Chemosh and Molech. “His heart was not wholly true to the LORD.” It is not that he stops believing in the LORD, but that he divides his heart. Divided loyalty is a form of idolatry.

God’s judgment is real: the kingdom will be torn. But even here, mercy shines. Not in Solomon’s lifetime, “for the sake of David,” and not the whole kingdom, “for the sake of Jerusalem which I have chosen.” God’s covenant with David is the reason the line continues. The promise holds, not because of Solomon’s merit, but because of God’s faithfulness.

The unit ends with a question the whole Old Testament will keep asking: if even Solomon fails, who can be the king God promised?
connection: Jesus is the king who did not divide his heart, who resisted every temptation (Matthew 4:1-11), and whose wisdom exceeds Solomon’s (Matthew 12:42). He is the true Son of David who will never fall. Where Solomon was led astray by foreign wives, the church is the bride of Christ, kept faithful by his grace (Ephesians 5:27). James 4:4-8 calls for single-hearted devotion. Hebrews 3:12 warns against an “evil, unbelieving heart.”
application:
Ask whether your heart is wholly true to the LORD or divided.

Look at what you have accumulated. Does anything have a hold on you?

Thank God that his promise rests on his faithfulness, and not on yours.
prayerPrompts: Ask God for an undivided heart.
Ask him to keep you from accumulating what turns you from him.
Thank him that his promise stands, even when people fail.
